exposure: mode of delivery (spontaneous vaginal delivery, instrumental vaginal delivery)
outcome: Length of hospital stay (LoS) after childbirth
proportion of women remaining admitted more than early discharge (ED) cutoffs
cohort: The study included 109,550 registered births in the Friuli Venezia-Giulia region of North-Eastern Italy from 2005 to 2015, focusing on mothers and newborns.
finding: The study revealed significant and extensive variability in the proportion of women exceeding early discharge benchmarks among different maternity centres in Friuli Venezia-Giulia, even after adjusting for clinical and socio-demographic factors, suggesting hospital-specific practices are a key determinant of Length of Stay.
mod_finding: The percentage of women staying longer than early discharge benchmarks varied widely by facility centre for both spontaneous vaginal deliveries (ranging from 32% to 97%) and instrumental vaginal deliveries (ranging from 15% to 64%), with a significantly decreasing trend in the proportion over the 11-year period for both delivery modes.
